## Security Review Summary

I performed a comprehensive security review of this OAuth service codebase, tracing data flows across all 10 files. I empirically verified each finding in Node.js before reporting it.

| Severity | Finding | Files |
|----------|---------|-------|
| 🔴 CRITICAL | **JWT `jku` key-fetch authentication bypass + SSRF** — `verifyExternalToken` reads the key URL from the unverified JWT header; `fetchKey` only does a string `startsWith` guard (bypassed via `https://keys.example.test@evil.com/...` or `https://keys.example.test.evil.com/...`) and follows redirects → attacker forges valid tokens | `src/oauth/token.js`, `src/oauth/jwks.js` |
| 🟠 HIGH | **OAuth `redirect_uri` prefix-match bypass** — `validateRedirect` uses `startsWith(client.baseUrl)`, bypassed by userinfo/subdomain tricks → authorization code sent to attacker host | `src/oauth/register.js` |
| 🟡 MEDIUM | **`redirect_uri` query/fragment not compared** — `exactRedirect` ignores `search` and `hash`, allowing arbitrary query parameters to a trusted callback host (code exfiltration via forwarding hosts) | `src/oauth/exact-redirect.js` |
| 🔵 LOW | **`verifyState` throws instead of returning false on mismatched length / missing input** → request failures / crash on the CSRF-state path | `src/oauth/state.js` |

**Deliberately not reported (verified false positives):**
- `pkce.js` uses SHA-256 in `base64url` — confirmed correct RFC 7636 S256 challenge method, not weak crypto.
- `http/safe-jwks.js` uses a fixed endpoint with `redirect:'manual'` — the *safe* reference pattern (actually reinforces that `jwks.js` is the vulnerable one).
- `config.js`, `logging.js`, `client-repo.js` — no exploitable issues; logging correctly omits sensitive values.

The machine-readable report is saved to `SECURITY_REVIEW.json` with `source_modified: false`. No audited source files were modified.
